findings.reason: the two clauses state incompatible bounds on the same compile, so a §4 node either deletes the xfail `because the cold compile now clears 60 s`, which the plan's own §3 says no lever reached (405 s at 132 after three levers and the tangent repair), or records a cache-served first call and leaves the suite red with no clause saying which outcome closes the section.
findings.text: §4 clause (1) says "the cold compile that fills the cache is recorded beside it and carries no bound", while clause (2) requires tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py::test_kernel_compile_growth to pass, and that test's own docstring says a strict unexpected pass "fires exactly when the cold read compiles within 60 s and 50 MB", its measurement child redirecting JAX_COMPILATION_CACHE_DIR to a fresh directory (tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py:2526-2530, :2576)

findings.reason: as written the section's binding memory clause is unmet by the mechanism the section adopts, and a worker who meets 60 s from the cache will still fail 64 GB through a bound the plan never shows anyone can move.
findings.text: §3 clause (1) requires "64 GB peak host memory" of the cache-served first call at the 2,132-node arm, but §0's own table (plan.html:44) records 381 GB peak at that arm and the coarse-tie run records that the memory stayed held for ~11,000 s in a 4-and-533-batch node loop after the compile, so the quantity is dominated by the loop's operand store, which neither the traced-body lever nor the pre-warm cache reduces

findings.reason: a node dispatched on §4 closes on (1)-(3) and drops a four-hour CPU regression arm, or carries two deliverables that one verdict cannot cover.
findings.text: §4 lists node (a) the compile clause and node (b) "a read-path regression arm with its own verdict" over tests/test_tracked_read.py, tests/test_bank_newton_step.py and tests/test_support_read.py as one section, while the section's done-when (plan.html:73) contains only (a)'s clauses (1)-(3), so (b)'s criterion ("every file has a completed pair and no failure id at head is absent from the base arm") exists in prose and in no gate

findings.reason: a 60 s first call is exactly what a cache hit or a skipped compilation also produces, so without a stated failing arm the section cannot distinguish a met bound from a guard that never ran.
findings.text: §4's three clauses bound a first call at 60 s, 50 MB and 64 GB at 132, 300 and 550 cells and name no arm that must miss those bounds, unlike §3(d)'s empty-cache arm that must exceed the miss budget and exit nonzero

findings.reason: the depends-on graph is what a dispatcher uses to order nodes and choose a base, and on this graph a §3 node can be dispatched onto a tree without the repair it is measured against.
findings.text: §3 states that node (c) "is built on the kernel as repaired by the polygon tangent repair of sub-millisecond-forward-path ... which landed on main at merge 681a6ecd2" and makes that merge the base whose control arm must miss 60 s, but its section declares data-links "kernel-compile-barrier#s2,kernel-compile-barrier#s5" and the plan's section-depends-on map gives no edge to sub-millisecond-forward-path; §6 declares exactly that edge for the same repair

findings.reason: the evidence fragment records the receipt path as its pointer, so a receipt in a pruned or quota-failing cache directory is a pointer a later reader cannot open, and moving it after the fact loses the runs that produced it.
findings.text: §3(b), (c) and (d) send their receipts to ~/.cache/nova-kernel-compile-barrier/point-program-attribution/, /one-traced-body/ and /cached-point-program/, a per-user cache directory, while the repository's binding receipts rule puts npz, gz and json receipts above a few MB under the GPFS evidence root resolved through nova/database/filepath.py, chosen specifically to sit outside every pruner root and distinct from ~/.cache (AGENTS.md, "Large receipts live on GPFS, not in git")

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the cited files, fragments, plans and commits all resolve, but three line anchors point at the wrong line inside a resolving file (polygonanalytic.py:2641, fixed_points.py:521, read_route/jets.py:321).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §4's done-when (1)-(3) declares no arm that must miss its 60 s / 50 MB / 64 GB bounds, so nothing shows the guard fires, and §3's clauses (1)-(3) otherwise carry declared controls (§3(d) empty-cache refusal, §6 truncated-tangent refusal, §3(c) 681a6ecd2 base arm).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §3(b), (c) and (d) put their receipts under ~/.cache/nova-kernel-compile-barrier/, against the repository's binding rule that large receipts live under the GPFS evidence root resolved through nova/database/filepath.py, outside every pruner root.
